title: Chamomile and honey soy candle
subtitle: A soft, warm-scented container candle for bedrooms
excerpt: A container soy candle scented with a chamomile and honey fragrance oil for a soft, warm, slightly sweet scent. Well-suited to bedrooms and reading corners. Makes one 200 ml jar candle.
sourceNotes: Soy wax container candle formulation: general candlemaking reference. Fragrance oil loading for soy wax: standard candle-making practice (6 to 8% by wax weight for container soy wax). IFRA guidelines for candle-grade fragrance oils.

recipe.yieldDescription: 1 jar candle (~150 g soy wax fill, 200 ml jar, ~35 to 40 burn hours)
recipe.batchNotes: Make four or five jars in a single melting session.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cure one week before the first burn.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keeps two years unlit in a cool, dark place. Fragrance oils are more stable than essential oils in wax and hold their scent well for 18 months. Discard if the wick has come loose from the base or the wax shows deep cracking.

glossaryTerms.definition: The percentage of fragrance or essential oil added to the wax weight. Container soy wax holds 6 to 8% fragrance oil before the oil begins to bleed out of the wax surface. The fragrance load affects scent throw: too low and the candle smells faint; too high and unbound fragrance pools on the surface.

content.text: A soft soy container candle for bedrooms and quiet rooms. The chamomile and honey fragrance oil gives a warm, slightly sweet scent that is calm rather than heavy. The
here is 7% of wax weight, which is within the standard range for container soy. Fragrance oils hold their scent through the pour and cure far more reliably than essential oils at the same loading.
Never leave a burning candle unattended or near flammable materials.

items.prepNote: chamomile and honey candle-grade fragrance oil; 7% of wax weight
pre-tabbed cotton wick for a 200 ml jar

content.text: Warm the jar in a 50°C oven for five minutes. Stick the wick tab to the jar base. Lay the wick across the centring bar so it stands centred and upright.
Melt the soy wax in the pouring pitcher over a bain-marie. Remove from the heat and cool to 60°C.

Stir in the fragrance oil at 60°C for one full minute. Pour slowly into the prepared jar. Leave to cool at room temperature overnight. Trim the wick to 5 mm once the wax is fully set. Cure for one week.
Allow the wax pool to reach the edges of the jar on the first burn before extinguishing. This prevents a wax tunnel forming around the wick on subsequent burns.
Two years in a cool, dark place. Fragrance oils are stable in soy wax for 18 months.
